title: Perimeter Arc Length on a Circular Disk
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: To construct an 80^\circ central angle on a circular disk of diameter 12 in., you mark an arc along the outer perimeter and connect its endpoints to the center. Find the required length of the arc, rounded to the nearest tenth of an inch.

steps.title: Determine the Radius of the Disk
steps.explanation: Halve the given diameter of 12 inches to obtain the radius r = 6 inches.
steps.why: The radius of a circle is half of its diameter.

steps.title: Convert the 80-Degree Central Angle to Radians
steps.explanation: Multiply 80 degrees by pi/180 and reduce the fraction by dividing numerator and denominator by 20.
steps.why: The formula s = r*theta requires the central angle to be expressed in radians.

steps.title: Calculate the Exact and Approximate Arc Length
steps.explanation: Multiply r = 6 in. by theta = 4*pi/9 rad to get 8*pi/3 in., which evaluates to approximately 8.4 inches when rounded to the nearest tenth.
steps.why: Evaluating 8*pi/3 numerically gives 8.37758..., which rounds to 8.4 at the first decimal place.
